Hi Sam / Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time to chat today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap:
- Primary use case: HealthCloud will surface patient records and clinical summaries to their care coordination app; some requests will include PHI (names, MRNs, encounter notes).
- Volume: pilot ~10k requests/month, production likely 200k+/month.
- Key ask: confirm whether Redwood can sign a BAA and which deployment options are eligible for PHI. Also requested: SOC 2 status and ability to complete HealthCloud's vendor security questionnaire.

What we can cover next:
1) Can you share the security questionnaire (if you already have it, please attach) and legal contact for the BAA?
2) I'll loop in our security lead to give the formal answers on SOC 2, encryption, and deployment boundaries.
3) I'll attach our BAA template and a short security one-pager for your security team to review.

Short answer up front: Redwood can sign a BAA. PHI usage requires a non-multi-tenant deployment — we support Dedicated (reserved capacity with network isolation) and Private (VPC or on-prem) for HIPAA workloads. Our hosted multi-tenant API is not intended for PHI without a private deployment / control plane. Details to follow from our security team.

Next steps: 
- Sam: please send over the questionnaire and legal contact (cc if possible).
- We'll aim to return the questionnaire within 3–5 business days after receiving it.
- If helpful, we can set up a 30-minute call between HealthCloud security and our security lead this week.

Attachments: Redwood_BAA_Template_v3.pdf, security_one_pager.pdf

Best,

Hi Sam / Emily —

Thanks for the questionnaire and the follow-up. Answers below (short form) and attaching a redacted SOC 2 Type II report (SOC2_report_redacted.pdf). Happy to join a short call if you want to walk through anything.

A) SOC 2 Type II: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II attestation covering security and availability controls. We can share a redacted report with customers under an NDA/SSAE channel — attached is a redacted copy for initial review.

B) Deployment / PHI boundaries: 
- Hosted (multi-tenant Redwood API): NOT approved for PHI. The hosted, shared control plane does not meet HealthCloud's PHI requirements. 
- Dedicated (reserved capacity / single-tenant GPU pools): Approved for PHI when configured with network isolation and customer tenancy. Data can be kept within the dedicated pool and excluded from our shared analytics.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Approved for PHI. Options: customer-managed VPC with private control plane, or on-prem package for fully air-gapped deployments. We support customer-managed KMS so you control encryption keys.

Technical controls / configuration considerations: 
- Encryption: TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest by default. For Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integration.
- KV cache & logs: For PHI workloads we recommend disabling prefix caching and KV cache persistence, and we can configure minimal logging (audit-only) with reduced retention. Access to audit logs is available to customers; we do not surface PHI in usage analytics for Dedicated/Private.
- Data residency: For Dedicated we can provision in specific cloud regions; Private on-prem obviously keeps data in your environment.

C) Timelines: 
- Vendor questionnaire: typical turnaround 3–7 business days depending on depth; I can own the technical sections and Neha can help with process/ops questions.
- BAA: we can execute a standard BAA within 3–10 business days depending on legal review and redlines. We will send a DocuSign link once Emily/legal confirm redlines.

Attachments: SOC2_report_redacted.pdf

If helpful, suggest we schedule a 30-minute session between HealthCloud security + procurement and our security lead to go over any high-risk items. Proposed times: Thu 19 Feb 10:00–10:30 PT or Fri 20 Feb 14:00–14:30 PT. Please let us know what works.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
